sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: This sound is unmistakable.
sentences.zh: 这个声音毋庸置疑。

sentences.en: Maybe you find it kind of lulling like I do since it signifies the end of a trip to the grocery store.
sentences.zh: 也许你和我一样，觉得它有催眠的效果，因为它标志着一趟超市购物之旅的结束。

sentences.en: You've found all the things on your list and now you get to just stand there and zone out for a second
sentences.zh: 你已经买齐了清单上的所有东西，现在你可以站在那里发呆一会儿，

sentences.en: or flip through a Bassett magazine while the checkout person does the work.
sentences.zh: 或者在收银员干活的时候翻翻杂志。

sentences.en: That's our new producer Katie Mingle.
sentences.zh: 那是我们的新制作人凯蒂·明格尔。

sentences.en: I myself find that sound a bit anxiety-inducing since it's also the sound of the total that I'm going to have to pay going up and up.
sentences.zh: 我个人觉得这个声音有点让人焦虑，因为它也是我不得不支付的总金额不断上涨的声音。

sentences.en: When I go to the grocery store and checkout, I'm utterly amazed at how well the skaters can read barcodes.
sentences.zh: 当我去超市结账时，我极其惊叹于收银员读取条形码的熟练程度。

sentences.en: No, I don't tell the checkout people.
sentences.zh: 不，我不会告诉收银员的。

sentences.en: My wife always did.
sentences.zh: 我妻子总是会说。

sentences.en: My husband here is the one that invented that barcode.
sentences.zh: 我身边的这位丈夫就是发明那个条形码的人。

sentences.en: And they just kind of look at you as if to say, yeah, I believe that.
sentences.zh: 他们看着你，仿佛在说，行吧，我相信。

sentences.en: But, of course, today, they would look at you as if to say, you mean there was a time they didn't have a barcode?
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，今天他们看着你，仿佛在说，你是说以前曾经没有条形码的时候？

sentences.en: It's hard to imagine now a world without barcodes.
sentences.zh: 现在很难想象一个没有条形码的世界。

sentences.en: A world without George Lauer.
sentences.zh: 一个没有乔治·劳尔的世界。

sentences.en: Well, hello.
sentences.zh: 你好啊。

sentences.en: I'm George J.
sentences.zh: 我是乔治·J·

sentences.en: Lauer.
sentences.zh: 劳尔。

sentences.en: I'm the one that invented the UPC barcode and symbol in 1973.
sentences.zh: 我是在1973年发明UPC条形码和符号的人。

sentences.en: Now, some of you might be saying to yourselves, I thought Joseph Woodland invented the barcode.
sentences.zh: 现在，你们中的有些人可能会对自己说，我以为条形码是约瑟夫·伍德兰发明的。

sentences.en: And if you're saying that to yourself, you are a nerd.
sentences.zh: 如果你在心里这么想，你就是一个书呆子。

sentences.en: And I love you for it.
sentences.zh: 我为此而喜欢你。

sentences.en: And just hold your nerd horses because we're getting to Woodland right now.
sentences.zh: 收起你那书呆子气的激动吧，因为我们现在就要讲到伍德兰。

sentences.en: It started the way a lot of things start, with people trying to make more money.
sentences.zh: 它的开始和很多事情的开始一样，人们试图赚更多的钱。

sentences.en: The grocery business decided that they needed some way to reduce their overhead.
sentences.zh: 杂货业决定，他们需要某种方式来减少管理费用。

sentences.en: One of the main places they felt they were losing money was the checkout line.
sentences.zh: 他们认为亏钱的主要地方之一就是结账排队。

sentences.en: They came up with the idea of having some kind of a scannable code.
sentences.zh: 他们想出了一个主意，就是某种可扫描的条码。

sentences.en: Which would move people more quickly through the line.
sentences.zh: 这可以让人更快地通过收银台。

sentences.en: One of the first people that started working on it was an engineer named Joseph Woodland.
sentences.zh: 最早开始研究这个问题的人之一是一位名叫约瑟夫·伍德兰的工程师。

sentences.en: After working on the Manhattan Project, Woodland moved on to develop an innovative way to produce elevator music.
sentences.zh: 在参与曼哈顿计划后，伍德兰转而开发一种创新的背景音乐制作方式。

sentences.en: He was jamming on this project, probably set to make a whole bunch of money,
sentences.zh: 他当时正热衷于这个项目，本可以赚一大笔钱，

sentences.en: until, and this is according to Woodland's New York Times obituary,
sentences.zh: 直到——根据伍德兰在《纽约时报》上的讣告记载——

sentences.en: his father forbid him from getting into the industry because it was controlled by the mob.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲禁止他涉足这个行业，因为它被黑帮控制了。

sentences.en: So Woodland moved on from elevator music to barcodes.
sentences.zh: 于是伍德兰从背景音乐转向了条形码。

sentences.en: He was trying to come up with a symbol that, when scanned, would translate to a series of numbers
sentences.zh: 他试图设计出这样一种符号：扫描时，它能转化为一系列数字，

sentences.en: that a computer could use to identify a product.
sentences.zh: 供计算机用来识别产品。

sentences.en: So one day he's sitting on the beach in Miami, Florida.
sentences.zh: 所以有一天，他坐在佛罗里达州迈阿密的海滩上。

sentences.en: So the legend goes.
sentences.zh: 传说就是这样的。

sentences.en: And Woodland's thinking about his days in the Boy Scouts and Morse code.
sentences.zh: 伍德兰想起了他在童子军的日子和摩斯密码。

sentences.en: As one tends to do on the beach.
sentences.zh: 人们在海滩上往往会这样。

sentences.en: And he's kind of absentmindedly drawing in the sand with his fingers,
sentences.zh: 他心不在焉地用手指在沙子上画着，

sentences.en: when suddenly he looks down and he's got it.
sentences.zh: 突然他低头一看，他成功了。

sentences.en: He's dragged his four fingers through the sand in the shape of concentric circles.
sentences.zh: 他用四根手指在沙子里拖出了同心圆的形状。

sentences.en: Instead of dot, dot, dot, dash, dash, dash, he thinks,
sentences.zh: 他想，与其用点、点、点、划、划、划，

sentences.en: I can use skinny and wide lines.
sentences.zh: 我可以利用细线和粗线。

sentences.en: Bullseye.
sentences.zh: 正中红心。

sentences.en: Bullseye.
sentences.zh: 正中红心。

sentences.en: The very first barcodes were in the shape of a bullseye.
sentences.zh: 最早的条形码是靶心形状的。

sentences.en: Actually, they didn't call them barcodes yet.
sentences.zh: 其实，当时他们还不叫它们条形码。

sentences.en: Woodland's invention was called a classifying apparatus and method.
sentences.zh: 伍德兰的发明被称为分类装置和方法。

sentences.en: I'm really glad that we don't call him that anymore.
sentences.zh: 我真高兴我们不再那样叫它了。

sentences.en: That was 1948.
And then for about 20 years, the bullseye idea gathered duSt.
sentences.zh: 然后在大约20年的时间里，靶心的想法被束之高阁。

sentences.en: The scanners and other equipment needed to put the system in place
sentences.zh: 实施该系统所需的扫描仪和其他设备

sentences.en: were just too expensive for any of it to be feasible.
sentences.zh: 实在太贵了，根本无法实行。

sentences.en: Fast forward to 1973.
sentences.zh: 时间快进到1973年。

sentences.en: The technology is now a bit more affordable,
sentences.zh: 这项技术现在变得更加实惠了，

sentences.en: and a group of supermarket executives led by a guy named Alan Haberman are like,
sentences.zh: 以一个叫艾伦·哈伯曼的人为首的一群超市高管觉得，

sentences.en: okay, barcode or bust, we're doing this.
sentences.zh: 好吧，要么搞定条形码，要么破产，我们干了。

sentences.en: By that time, there were a few other designs out there, but none were perfect.
sentences.zh: 那时候，还有其他一些设计，但没有一个完美。

sentences.en: So they put together a list of qualities that their ideal barcode would have
sentences.zh: 于是他们列出了一份理想条形码应具备的品质清单，

sentences.en: and asked 14 different companies to come up with a proposal.
sentences.zh: 并要求14家不同的公司提出方案。

sentences.en: Could be no larger than one and a half square inches.
sentences.zh: 尺寸不得大于一平方英寸半。

sentences.en: Had to have a good enough depth of field.
sentences.zh: 必须有足够好的景深。

sentences.en: They could read about a foot and a half above the scanner.
sentences.zh: 它们可以在扫描仪上方约一英尺半的地方被读取。

sentences.en: Had to be omnidirectional.
sentences.zh: 必须是全向的。

sentences.en: That's George Lohrer again.
sentences.zh: 又是乔治·洛雷尔。

sentences.en: He was working at IBM at the time,
sentences.zh: 他当时在IBM工作，

sentences.en: which was one of the companies competing to make the best barcode.
sentences.zh: 该公司是竞争制造最佳条形码的公司之一。

sentences.en: And most people thought that a circular design like Woodland's
sentences.zh: 大多数人认为，像伍德兰那样的圆形设计

sentences.en: would probably work best because of the way the scanners worked.
sentences.zh: 可能会效果最好，因为扫描仪的工作方式。

sentences.en: In those days, just about every scanner was a single line.
sentences.zh: 在那个年代，几乎每个扫描仪都是单条扫描线。

sentences.en: And you can just picture that if you had a single line
sentences.zh: 你可以想象一下，如果你有一条单线，

sentences.en: and it was going in the direction of the bar, it would not read all the bars.
sentences.zh: 并且它沿着条纹的方向行进，它就无法读取所有的条纹。

sentences.en: Woodland's original circular design solved this
sentences.zh: 伍德兰最初的圆形设计解决了这个问题，

sentences.en: because it could be read from any direction.
sentences.zh: 因为它可以在任何方向被读取。

sentences.en: That meant the checkout person didn't have to take your bag of Cheetos
sentences.zh: 这意味着收银员不必拿起你那一袋奇多，

sentences.en: and turn it in just the right way before it could pass over the scanner.
sentences.zh: 在它通过扫描仪之前把它转到正确的方向。

sentences.en: But George didn't think the bullseye symbol would work.
sentences.zh: 但乔治认为靶心符号行不通。

sentences.en: I couldn't support that as the solution to what the grocery industry wanted.
sentences.zh: 我不能支持它作为杂货业想要的东西的解决方案。

sentences.en: Because to me, there was no way that it would fulfill their specifications.
sentences.zh: 因为在我看来，它绝不可能满足他们的规格要求。

sentences.en: My integrity just would not let me come up with a bunch of bull.
sentences.zh: 我的正直不容许我搞出一堆废话。

sentences.en: So George went back to the drawing table.
sentences.zh: 于是乔治回到了图纸前。

sentences.en: My wife said I came back and I would work on it day and night.
sentences.zh: 我妻子说我回来后日夜不停地工作。

sentences.en: Come back at night and, again, most of us was thinking, arithmetic,
sentences.zh: 晚上回来，而且，我们大多数人都在想，算术，

sentences.en: trying to prove that this would work.
sentences.zh: 试图证明这是行得通的。

sentences.en: Also, I have to admit, I had to disprove that some of the others wouldn't work.
sentences.zh: 另外，我必须承认，我不得不反证其他一些方案是行不通的。

sentences.en: He ultimately came up with a rectangular barcode that fit more code into less space,
sentences.zh: 他最终设计出了一个矩形条形码，能在更小的空间里容纳更多的代码，

sentences.en: which was crucial since grocery manufacturers were already grumbling
sentences.zh: 这至关重要，因为杂货制造商已经在抱怨

sentences.en: about having to make room for this new symbol on their packaging.
sentences.zh: 必须在包装上为这个新符号腾出空间。

sentences.en: But there was still the issue of the one-line scanner.
sentences.zh: 但单线扫描仪的问题依然存在。

sentences.en: Somehow we got the idea that if we used an X for the scan pattern,
sentences.zh: 不知怎的，我们有了一个想法，如果我们用X字形作为扫描图案，

sentences.en: which could be developed very easily with a pair of mirrors...
sentences.zh: 这可以通过一对镜子非常容易地实现……

sentences.en: Then, the barcode could be read by the scanner no matter which way it was oriented as it passed.
sentences.zh: 那么，无论条形码在通过时朝向哪个方向，扫描仪都能读取它。

sentences.en: So even though Woodland came up with the original idea of using lines of various widths,
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管伍德兰想出了用不同宽度线条的最初创意，

sentences.en: George Lohrer did more than just change that shape from a circle to a rectangle.
sentences.zh: 乔治·洛雷尔所做的不仅仅是将形状从圆形改为矩形。

sentences.en: He improved on the symbol, the code behind the symbol,
sentences.zh: 他改进了符号、符号背后的代码，

sentences.en: and the scanners that read the symbol.
sentences.zh: 以及读取该符号的扫描仪。

sentences.en: Even Joe Woodland thought so.
sentences.zh: 连乔治·伍德兰也这么认为。

sentences.en: Joe Woodland was very enthusiastic.
sentences.zh: 乔治·伍德兰非常热情。

sentences.en: He worked with me.
sentences.zh: 他和一起我工作。

sentences.en: In fact, he wrote the actual proposal for the submission to the grocery industry.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他亲自撰写了提交给杂货业的提案。

sentences.en: But it was my invention of the particular symbol and barcode that we see today.
sentences.zh: 但今天我们看到的特定符号和条形码是我的发明。

sentences.en: The Symbol Selection Committee unanimously voted for George Lohrer's rectangular symbol and code.
sentences.zh: 符号选择委员会一致投票通过了乔治·洛雷尔的矩形符号和代码。

sentences.en: They called it the Universal Product Code, or UPC.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为通用产品代码，简称UPC。

sentences.en: And a year later, in 1974, a pack of Wrigley's chewing gum became the first item to ever be scanned with the UPC barcode.
sentences.zh: 一年后的1974年，一包箭牌口香糖成为了第一个被扫描UPC条形码的商品。

sentences.en: If barcodes hadn't been invented, the entire layout and the architecture of commerce would have been different.
sentences.zh: 如果没有发明条形码，商业的整体布局和架构将会完全不同。

sentences.en: The impacts are very difficult to overestimate.
sentences.zh: 其影响怎么高估都不为过。

sentences.en: My name is Sanjay Sarma.
sentences.zh: 我叫桑杰·萨马。

sentences.en: I'm a professor of mechanical engineering at MIT.
sentences.zh: 我是麻省理工学院机械工程教授。

sentences.en: Sanjay Sarma has also worked with an organization called GS1.
sentences.zh: 桑杰·萨马还曾与一个名为GS1的组织合作。

sentences.en: That stands for Global Standards 1.
sentences.zh: 那是全球标准1组织的缩写。

sentences.en: And if you need a barcode on your product, you have to go through GS1 to get it.
sentences.zh: 如果你的产品需要条形码，你必须通过GS1来获取。

sentences.en: Imagine if the telephone numbers weren't standardized, right?
sentences.zh: 想象一下，如果电话号码没有标准化，对吧？

sentences.en: And you didn't have area codes, and two people could have the same phone number.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有区号，两个人可能会有相同的电话号码。

sentences.en: You know, you need standards.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你需要标准。

sentences.en: When barcodes became the standard, they didn't just make checkout lines faster.
sentences.zh: 当条形码成为标准时，它们不仅加快了结账速度。

sentences.en: They allowed stores to keep track of huge amounts of inventory and to collect data on what we were buying.
sentences.zh: 它们还允许商店追踪海量库存，并收集我们购买行为的数据。

sentences.en: Data they could use to keep us coming back for more.
sentences.zh: 他们可以用这些数据吸引我们不断回头购买。

sentences.en: Without barcodes.
sentences.zh: 如果没有条形码。

sentences.en: Super stores might not exiSt.
sentences.zh: 超级大卖场可能就不会存在。

sentences.en: But equally, you know, a small store might need more employees to run it.
sentences.zh: 但同样地，你知道，一家小店可能需要更多员工来经营。

sentences.en: It's like the grease that makes the machine run.
sentences.zh: 它就像让机器运转的润滑油。

sentences.en: It's one of the key, you know, elements of efficiency in our capitalistic system.
sentences.zh: 它是我们资本主义制度中效率的关键要素之一。

sentences.en: And when you put it like that, you can see why for some people,
sentences.zh: 当你这样说的时候，你就会明白为什么对某些人来说，

sentences.en: the barcode has come to represent everything they hate about capitalism and consumerism.
sentences.zh: 条形码已经成为他们痛恨资本主义和消费主义的一切的象征。

sentences.en: You can get wrapped candies of every kind.
sentences.zh: 你可以买到各种各样的散装糖果。

sentences.en: Bubblegum, lollipops, fun-sized candy bars.
sentences.zh: 泡泡糖、棒棒糖、迷你糖果条。

sentences.en: Just $1.89.
sentences.zh: 只要1.89美元。

sentences.en: When I was a punk kid, if a band's album had a barcode on it,
sentences.zh: 当我还是个朋克小子时，如果某个乐队的专辑上有条形码，

sentences.en: we knew they were complete sellouts.
sentences.zh: 我们就知道他们彻底出卖了灵魂。

sentences.en: It ain't the barcode's fault.
sentences.zh: 这不是条形码的错。

sentences.en: But it's become the symbol or the glyph of technology we're afraid of or don't understand
sentences.zh: 但它已经成了我们所恐惧、不理解的技术的符号或图腾，

sentences.en: or being a cog in a wheel in a larger monolithic machine.
sentences.zh: 或者是一个更庞大、铁板一块的机器中的一颗螺丝钉。

sentences.en: The matrix, if you will.
sentences.zh: 也就是所谓的母体。

sentences.en: Oh, I will, Jerry Whiting.
sentences.zh: 哦，我会的，杰里·惠丁。

sentences.en: My name is Jerry Whiting.
sentences.zh: 我叫杰里·惠丁。

sentences.en: I am the founder of Azalea Software here in Seattle, Washington.
sentences.zh: 我是华盛顿州西雅图市阿扎利阿软件公司的创始人。

sentences.en: I've been writing software that prints barcodes for 25 years now.
sentences.zh: 我编写打印条形码的软件已经25年了。

sentences.en: They aren't bad.
sentences.zh: 它们并不坏。

sentences.en: They aren't good.
sentences.zh: 它们也说不上好。

sentences.en: They're just tools.
sentences.zh: 它们只是工具。

sentences.en: But most people look at them and don't even know where to start.
sentences.zh: 但大多数人看着它们，甚至不知道从哪里开始。

sentences.en: So let's demystify for a minute and look at what's inside the barcode.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们花点时间揭开它的神秘面纱，看看条形码里面有什么。

sentences.en: Again, what we're talking about here is the UPC barcode that George Lohrer invented.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我们在这里讨论的是乔治·洛雷尔发明的UPC条形码。

sentences.en: This is the barcode that you and I and everyone in the world has had the most interaction with.
sentences.zh: 这是你、我和世界上每个人互动最多的条形码。

sentences.en: The UPC barcode is divided into two halves.
sentences.zh: UPC条形码分为两半。

sentences.en: It's actually two barcodes sitting right next to each other.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是紧挨在一起的两个条形码。

sentences.en: You can see this visually because there are these longer bars that come down in the middle and on each side.
sentences.zh: 你可以从视觉上看到这一点，因为中间和两侧有这些延伸下来的更长的条纹。

sentences.en: Those are called the guard bars.
sentences.zh: 那些叫作护条。

sentences.en: The guard bars tell the scanner that the code is starting and ending.
sentences.zh: 护条告诉扫描仪条形码从哪开始，到哪结束。

sentences.en: The left half of the barcode tells you who the manufacturer is and the right half tells you which particular product it is.
sentences.zh: 条形码的左半部分告诉你制造商是谁，右半部分告诉你具体是什么产品。

sentences.en: And this was something I didn't realize.
sentences.zh: 这也是我以前没意识到的一点。

sentences.en: The scanner is reading both the white and the dark lines.
sentences.zh: 扫描仪同时在读取白色线条和深色线条。

sentences.en: To understand the scanner, just consider yourself in a dark room where the wall behind you has bars painted on it.
sentences.zh: 为了理解扫描仪的工作原理，你可以把自己想象在一个黑屋子里，身后的墙上画着条纹。

sentences.en: And you took a flashlight and shined it over your head across the bars.
sentences.zh: 你拿着一个手电筒，把光照过头顶，扫过那些条纹。

sentences.en: You would see the room get a little lighter when you were over the white bars.
sentences.zh: 当光扫过白条时，你会发现房间变亮了一点。

sentences.en: And it would get dark when it was over the dark bars.
sentences.zh: 而当它扫到黑条时，房间就会变暗。

sentences.en: Black lines that don't reflect the laser light back to the scanner register as a one.
sentences.zh: 无法将激光反射回扫描仪的黑线代表数字1。

sentences.en: White lines equal zero.
sentences.zh: 白线等于0。

sentences.en: There are actually 95 evenly spaced columns on a UPC barcode.
sentences.zh: 通用产品代码（UPC）条形码上实际上有95个等间距的列。

sentences.en: A thick black line is actually a bunch of ones right next to each other.
sentences.zh: 一条粗黑线其实就是一堆紧挨在一起的1。

sentences.en: The computer adds all that together and you get a string of 12 numbers.
sentences.zh: 计算机把所有这些加在一起，你就会得到一串12位数字。

sentences.en: This number goes to the computer.
sentences.zh: 这个数字会被发送到计算机。

sentences.en: The computer now looks up in its table to get the information, such as what is the product, how much they're charging for it.
sentences.zh: 计算机现在在其表格中查找相关信息，比如这是什么产品，售价是多少。

sentences.en: But that is not in the barcode.
sentences.zh: 但这些信息并不在条形码里。

sentences.en: The only thing that's in the barcode is where the computer should look.
sentences.zh: 条形码里唯一包含的信息是计算机应该去哪里查找。

sentences.en: This number is also printed below the barcode just in case the scanner isn't working.
sentences.zh: 这个数字也会被打印在条形码下方，以防扫描仪无法工作。

sentences.en: Which, for me, really makes the whole mystery a little anticlimactic.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这确实让整个谜团显得有点虎头蛇尾。

sentences.en: I mean, it's right there.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它就摆在那里。

sentences.en: So, when most people until recently thought of barcodes, they thought of something that was a combination of bars and stripes.
sentences.zh: 因此，直到最近，当大多数人想到条形码时，他们想到的都是由条纹和线条组合而成的东西。

sentences.en: More recently, two-dimensional barcodes, which are, they look like crossword puzzles, have emerged.
sentences.zh: 最近，出现了看起来像填字游戏的二维条形码。

sentences.en: The most popular being QR barcodes, quick response, that are scanned by cell phones.
sentences.zh: 最受欢迎的是可以通过手机扫描的QR码，即快速响应码。

sentences.en: We've all seen these, and maybe a few of us have actually bothered to pull out our cell phones and download the app required to scan them.
sentences.zh: 我们都见过这些，也许我们当中有少数人真的特意掏出手机，下载了扫描它们所需的应用程序。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's something about them that I find kind of lame or annoying.
sentences.zh: 对，它们身上有些东西让我觉得有点无聊或烦人。

sentences.en: You know, it's like, no, Chili's, I don't want more info on the Bloomin' Onion.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这就好比，不，奇利餐厅，我不需要关于盛开洋葱花的更多信息。

sentences.en: Well, if you did, you might know that the Bloomin' Onion is from Outback.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果你知道了，你可能会发现盛开洋葱花是澳拜客牛排馆的。

sentences.en: So, anyway, I googled, why are QR codes lame?
sentences.zh: 所以，不管怎样，我谷歌了一下：为什么QR码这么无聊？

sentences.en: And I got a bunch of articles basically saying, they're actually really useful.
sentences.zh: 然后我看到了一堆文章，基本上都在说，它们其实非常有用。

sentences.en: They're just being misused.
sentences.zh: 只是它们被滥用了。

sentences.en: Mostly by advertisers who've just started slapping them on every single thing.
sentences.zh: 主要是被那些开始把它们胡乱贴在每一样东西上的广告商滥用了。

sentences.en: But Jerry Whiting, he still believes in them.
sentences.zh: 但杰里·惠丁仍然对它们深信不疑。

sentences.en: The nice thing about QR barcodes is, they are not just a lookup number to an external database.
sentences.zh: QR码的好处在于，它们不仅仅是外部数据库的查询编号。

sentences.en: Yes, it can be a chunk of text.
sentences.zh: 是的，它可以是一段文本。

sentences.en: It can be a URL.
sentences.zh: 它可以是一个网址。

sentences.en: It can be a whole lot of different things.
sentences.zh: 它可以是许许多多不同的东西。

sentences.en: But there is no central authority that tells you what or how to do anything.
sentences.zh: 但没有哪个中央权威机构告诉你该做什么或怎么做。

sentences.en: Meaning you don't have to go through GS1 to get a QR code,
sentences.zh: 这意味着你不需要通过GS1来获取QR码，

sentences.en: which lets people do stuff like make a giant picture of Amy Goodman's face entirely out of QR codes.
sentences.zh: 这让人们能够做出诸如用纯QR码拼出埃米·古德曼巨幅头像这样的作品。

sentences.en: This is my QR code, Amy Goodman portrait, made with 2,304 unique QR codes that link to nine years of Democracy Now!
sentences.zh: 这是我的QR码埃米·古德曼肖像，由2304个独特的QR码组成，链接到《现在的民主！》

sentences.en: videos.
sentences.zh: 九年来的视频。

sentences.en: Besides the QR code, Laura and Woodland's original barcodes have spawned a bunch of other barcodes.
sentences.zh: 除了QR码，劳拉和伍德兰最初发明的条形码还衍生出了许多其他条形码。

sentences.en: They're used for all sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 它们被用于各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: There's code 128, which is mostly used for packaging and shipping.
sentences.zh: 比如128码，主要用于包装和运输。

sentences.en: There's PostNet, which is used by the post office to sort mail.
sentences.zh: 还有邮网码，被邮局用来分拣邮件。

sentences.en: There are barcodes that use radio frequencies to send out data.
sentences.zh: 还有使用射频来发送数据的条形码。

sentences.en: They're called RFID tags, and they aren't really barcodes at all.
sentences.zh: 它们被称为RFID标签，其实根本算不上条形码。

sentences.en: They just get put in the same category because, like barcodes, they're being used to keep track of inventory.
sentences.zh: 它们只是被归入同一类别，因为和条形码一样，它们被用来追踪库存。

sentences.en: With a grocery cart full of RFID-tagged items, one could conceivably wheel their cart through a big hoop
sentences.zh: 推着一整车装有RFID标签商品的购物车，人们完全可以推着车穿过一个大环形装置，

sentences.en: that would read all the contents all at once, basically eliminating the checkout line entirely
sentences.zh: 该装置可以一次性读取所有商品的内容，从而基本上彻底省去了结账排队，

sentences.en: and allowing more people to pass through stores even more quickly so that we can all buy more stuff.
sentences.zh: 并允许更多人更快地通过商店，好让我们所有人都能买更多的东西。

sentences.en: Barcodes help us keep track of prescriptions, library books, luggage, endangered animals.
sentences.zh: 条形码帮助我们追踪处方药、图书馆藏书、行李、濒危动物。

sentences.en: There are so many barcodes on so many things that, according to Jerry Whiting,
sentences.zh: 有太多的条形码贴在太多的东西上，以至于根据杰里·惠丁的说法，

sentences.en: When future archaeologists come across remnants of our backward-ass civilization
sentences.zh: 当未来的考古学家偶然发现我们这个落后文明的残余，

sentences.en: and they stumble across a barcode, they're going to sign it religious significance
sentences.zh: 并且他们偶然发现一个条形码时，他们会赋予它宗教意义，

sentences.en: if they don't understand the supply chain.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不理解供应链的话。

sentences.en: We had no idea how far it was going to go.
sentences.zh: 我们当时根本不知道它会发展到多远。

sentences.en: We thought it would stay just within the grocery industry.
sentences.zh: 我们以为它只会局限在杂货行业。

sentences.en: But of course, it didn't just stay in the grocery industry.
sentences.zh: 但当然，它并没有仅仅局限在杂货行业。

sentences.en: It actually went way beyond that, all the way to conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 它实际上远远超出了这个范畴，甚至延伸到了阴谋论。

sentences.en: There is, in fact, a silly conspiracy theory that all barcodes have the number of the beast,
sentences.zh: 事实上，有一个愚蠢的阴谋论称，所有条形码里都编码了野兽的数字，

sentences.en: 666, encoded into them.
Yeah, it has to do with those guard bars that come at the beginning, middle, and end of every barcode.
sentences.zh: 对，这与出现在每个条形码开头、中间和结尾的那些护条有关。

sentences.en: And it's basically true that there are three 6s coded into the guard bars.
sentences.zh: 而且护条里确实编码了三个6，这基本是事实。

sentences.en: The answer to why is a bit technical.
sentences.zh: 至于原因，答案有点技术性。

sentences.en: You can read about it on George Lohr's personal website in the FAQ section if you want.
sentences.zh: 如果你想了解，可以在乔治·洛尔的个人网站的常见问题解答部分阅读相关内容。

sentences.en: But as Exhibit B, I submit George himself.
sentences.zh: 但作为B证据，我请出了乔治本人。

sentences.en: Well, hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: I'm George J.
sentences.zh: 我是乔治·J·

sentences.en: Lohr.
sentences.zh: 洛尔。

sentences.en: After we were done with our interview, he was talking a little bit more about his job at IBM.
sentences.zh: 在我们采访结束后，他多聊了聊他在IBM的工作。

sentences.en: And then when I'd come home at night, I'd go, oh, I had a tough day.
sentences.zh: 然后当我晚上回家时，我会说，哦，我今天过得很艰难。

sentences.en: Well, my poor wife was taking care of four kids.
sentences.zh: 而我可怜的妻子还要照顾四个孩子。

sentences.en: And then he started talking about his wife and his kids.
sentences.zh: 然后他开始谈论他的妻子和孩子。

sentences.en: She had the hard job, believe me.
sentences.zh: 相信我，她才承担了最辛苦的工作。

sentences.en: She gave up her career, which was a teaching career, in order to take care of the kids.
sentences.zh: 她放弃了自己的职业——教师职业，来照顾孩子们。

sentences.en: And believe me, we are so proud of those kids.
sentences.zh: 相信我，我们为那些孩子感到无比骄傲。

sentences.en: Really, they are.
sentences.zh: 真的，他们确实如此。

sentences.en: You just couldn't ask for better kids.
sentences.zh: 你简直找不到更好的孩子了。

sentences.en: And this is because my wife spent her career raising those kids.
sentences.zh: 这是因为我妻子把她的职业生涯都花在了抚养这些孩子上。

sentences.en: I'm just so lucky.
sentences.zh: 我真是太幸运了。

sentences.en: So, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不知道。

sentences.en: Does that sound like a Satan worshiper to you guys?
sentences.zh: 在你们看来，这听起来像是个崇拜撒旦的人吗？

sentences.en: My daughter has a bachelor's degree.
sentences.zh: 我女儿有学士学位。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Katie Mingle with Sam Greenspan, Avery Truffleman, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%无形》由凯蒂·明格制作，参与者还有萨姆·格林斯潘、艾弗里·特鲁夫曼以及我，罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Jenny Morgan for production help.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢珍妮·摩根对制作提供的帮助。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 Local Public Radio KALW in San Francisco and produced at the offices of Arxon,
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山91.7地方公共广播电台KALW的一个项目，制作地点位于阿克松的办公室，

sentences.en: an architecture firm in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 阿克松是一家位于美丽的加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心的建筑事务所。

sentences.en: He has a bachelor's degree in engineering from Charlotte.
sentences.zh: 他拥有夏洛特分校的工程学学士学位。

sentences.en: Our youngest son has a Ph.D.
sentences.zh: 我们的小儿子拥有

sentences.en: from state.
sentences.zh: 州立大学的博士学位。

sentences.en: You can find the show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在脸书上找到并关注这个节目。

sentences.en: We all tweet.
sentences.zh: 我们都在发推特。

sentences.en: You can find us.
sentences.zh: 你可以找到我们。

sentences.en: We have a Tumblr.
sentences.zh: 我们有汤博乐博客。

sentences.en: It's fantastic.
sentences.zh: 棒极了。

sentences.en: But if you want a link to George Lohr's self-published autobiography called Engineering Was Fun!
sentences.zh: 但如果你想要乔治·洛尔自费出版的名为《工程学真好玩！》的自传的链接，

sentences.en: Exclamation point.
sentences.zh: 感叹号。

sentences.en: Go to 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 请访问99pi.org。
